answer: The mirror-ocean terrace test binds one identity to one built terrace: the claimant builds a terrace above a named ocean cove, sets a mirror to catch the sunrise, and records how light crosses the terrace floor at noon. Two terrace wardens repeat the measure, check the stones against the terrace register, and confirm the reading within three days. A moved mirror, a copied reading, or a measure taken away from the ocean voids the season, burns a 110-credit stake, and bars the sponsor for two years. One honest test costs 110 credits; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 terraces built and measured by hand.
